targets.title: Factorial Survey Experiments to Predict Real-World Behavior: A Cautionary Tale from Hiring Studies.
targets.evidence_quote:
In order to test the labour queue–derived expectation that the dropout penalty is more
pronounced in fields where higher education is more prevalent, we replicate the regression
models presented in Forster and Neugebauer (2024), but additionally allow the estimate of
interest to vary by occupational field through an included interaction term.
targets.outcome_computational_quote:

targets.outcome_robustness_quote:
Our analyses show that the original results do
not withstand all robustness checks and that theoretically derived effect heterogeneities across
occupational fields provide more nuanced explanations.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The reanalysis goes directly to an omitted comparison and models with occupational-field interactions rather than testing recovery of original numbers. Alternative analyses qualify the central conclusion.

reasoning: Version 2 source PDF matches title and all three authors. Reanalyses use the original publicly available data, so this is a reproduction despite the authors calling it replication. The 2025 response is background, not a second target.
